# A - Requirements Review

Nouns - Patient, Practitioner, Appointment, Status, History & Staff.

Verbs - Register, Search, Create, Cancel, Update, View, Modify & Prevent.

Business Rules - No two active appointments may conflict for the same practitioner per FR-05, appointments that are cancelled are retained as per FR-07, relevant data must be preserved between sessions as per FR-08

# G - Python Skeletons

Create simple Patient, Practitioner and Appointment class skeletons.

# H - Consistency Check

Skeletons and CRC cards match up, Patient class only handles its own data, Practitioner class owns all conflict checks against its own appointments as per requirement 5. Appointments own its status matching with requirements 6 and 7. No logic for booking, persistence or validation, as at this stage we are looking at structure and not full behaviour.

# Reflection

Although the temptation of manager classes looked very useful, no confirmed requirements were actually stated to require that extra layer of architecture. The concept is an overdesign by suggesting a notification manager and clinic controller which currently are a bit beyond the scope and features the client has already asked for. The functional requirements list has been the core to shaping the final model and the classes whose responsibility could be traced back to the functional requirements were noted and everything else ignored.
